responsibilities.label: Hosted monitoring service
responsibilities.explanation: The provider runs the monitoring system. You still maintain the software that sends data from your app and servers, check that the data is useful and avoid slowing down your app. Monitoring data is also called telemetry.
values: Provider runs the selected hosting option

responsibilities.label: Collecting monitoring data
responsibilities.explanation: Connect code libraries or collection programs to send monitoring data. Logs record events, metrics measure values over time and traces show a request's path through connected apps. Check for missing data and broken connections. Automatic collection still needs setup and testing.

responsibilities.label: Protecting sensitive data
responsibilities.explanation: Keep secrets and personal data out of monitoring records. Set supported filters and access rules, then test that sensitive values are removed. Provider filtering tools do not replace your own rules about what data may be collected.

responsibilities.label: Choosing what data to keep
responsibilities.explanation: Choose which records to collect and how long to keep them. Sampling means keeping only a selection rather than every record; it affects which problems you can investigate. More history or measurements with many unique values can increase costs.

responsibilities.label: Alerts and reliability goals
responsibilities.explanation: Choose which problems need attention, when to send alerts and who receives them. Set reliability goals, such as how often requests should succeed. The provider does not know the impact on your users or decide who should respond.

responsibilities.label: Access rules
responsibilities.explanation: Keep live-app monitoring data separate from development and test data. Protect access keys and give each person or program only the access it needs. Available team and permission features depend on the product and plan.

responsibilities.label: Fixing problems
responsibilities.explanation: The platform can detect problems, send alerts and help with investigation. Your team still works out the effect on users, coordinates the response, repairs the app and checks that it works again.
